note: Primitive camping at the area headquarters off Route TT, on the upland edge of the Mississippi bottoms: a small tree-ringed gravel loop off the north end of the headquarters gravel lot. No tables or hookups. Camping is also allowed on or beside the area's other parking lots, but from October 15 to the close of the duck season only at this headquarters lot. No unattended campfires. The wetland units, levee roads and river are east of here; large parts are closed to all use in waterfowl season. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC designates the camp at headquarters (map Primitive Camping symbol by the office, GIS point on a small gravel loop off the HQ gravel lot); it lies outside both the refuge and the waterfowl-hunting-zone hatching and is the one place camping stays open in duck season. Stays. Phone matches.
flags: LOT RULE - STAYS: the brochure says 'Camping is allowed on or adjacent to parking lots... From October 15 to the close of the area's duck season, camping is only allowed at the gravel parking lot at the area headquarters.' That wording alone would be a lot-camping drop, but the 10/11/2022 map puts a Primitive Camping symbol beside the Conservation Area Office and its Parking Lot symbol, and GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point at 39.54443,-91.16578. On imagery that point is inside a narrow U-shaped gravel loop about 60 m long and 25 m wide, ringed by trees, running north off the gravel lot (GIS lot 2628, 39 m south) that sits 150 m north of the headquarters building - a small purpose-made camping loop, not just the lot. No pads or tables visible.

REFUGE / ZONES: on the map the headquarters corner (off Route TT at the north-west edge, west of the area road) is outside both hatchings - 'Waterfowl Hunting Zone (Closed to all use at 1pm) Oct 15. - end of North Zone Season' and 'Waterfowl Refuge Closed to all use Oct 15. to Mar 1.' - which cover the bottoms to the east. The stored season note ('Portions of the area are closed to protect waterfowl, October 15 through March 1', manual) is true of the area but not of the camp; the season group is manual so nothing was written - the duck-season rule went in the note instead.

FLOODING / LEVEES: the camp is reached from Route TT on the paved area road without crossing a levee; the 35 miles of levees and the units are east of it. Whether the headquarters bench itself floods is not stated on any page read. No closure posted now.
PIN: stored 39.54443,-91.16578 = GIS camping point, on the gravel loop. No move.

PHONE: stored 573-248-2530 matches the page's 'For more information call (573) 248-2530'. The brochure also gives the area office: Ted Shanks Conservation Area, 3643 Pike 145, Ashburn, (573) 754-6171.
NOT WATERFRONT stands: the Mississippi is more than 1.5 km east across the units (map scale); small ponds 150 m south of the headquarters are not camp frontage.
No split (one designated point). Dupont Reservation CA (13861) is 2.1 km north, a separate area.
